text:
maria: Heads-up — telemetry flagged a spike in fallback rate for 'starter' tier in eu-west this morning. Looks like more than expected are dropping to the smaller variant.
kai: Which fallback path specifically? small->tiny or small->medium?
anil: Logs show majority are small->tiny with a tool-calling error after the switch. Error is `unsupported_tokenizer` in the toolchain layer.
maria: Exactly. Repro steps: call with content-length ~6k tokens, primary model = `redwood-small-16k`, fallback = `redwood-tiny-8k`. When routed, tool-call payloads that include `tool_id` + structured args fail parse.
lee: That smells like tokenizer divergence: medium/large use SentencePiece, tiny uses custom BPE. We documented some token-id differences earlier.
sylvia: We already have a compatibility matrix but it's sparse for tool-calling parity. Current matrix marks tokenizer parity only at a model-family level, not by context-length profile.
kai: Are we sure context length is the trigger? Could also be a serialization mismatch from the runtime when we strip KV cache on fallback.
anil: Reproduced locally: when fallback occurs mid-stream, the runtime re-encodes the tool args using target model tokenizer and a field `metadata.format=v1` gets set. tiny expects `v0`.
maria: So two problems: tokenizer differences + metadata/versioning for tool-call payloads. Both cause the call router to reject.
lee: Small mitigation: add a routing policy that prevents fallback to variants with different tokenizer families when the request includes `tool_call=true`. We could make that a hard rule for starter tier.
kai: That helps but starter tier was deliberately allowed cheaper fallbacks to save cost. Product will push back if we make tool-calls more expensive.
sylvia: UX idea: Console should expose a per-route toggle "preserve-tool-calls-on-fallback" with a cost estimate and telemetry. That lets teams opt-in to stricter fallbacks.
maria: Good. For immediate ops: can we add an alert rule on fallback_rate_by_route where tool_call=true and tokenizer_mismatch=true -> P1?
oncall-bot: Incident threshold update suggestion queued: increase sensitivity for eu-west starter-tier fallback anomalies.
anil: I can add a quick rule in Grafana: `sum(rate(fallback_total{region="eu-west",tier="starter",tool_call="true"}[5m])) > 0.01` then page.
kai: Also need a dashboard panel showing tokenizer family per active variant and last-known parity matrix hash, so SRE can see which variants are safe to fallback to.
lee: Agreed. For rollout UX, we should extend the rollout UI to show "compatibility gates" — e.g., tokenizer parity, context-length fallback trim behavior, tool-calling metadata parity. When a canary variant fails a gate, block automatic promotion.
sylvia: That ties to the eval infra. We can auto-run a quick parity check (tokenizer decode/encode roundtrip + small tool-call simulation) when onboarding a variant. Add a `compat-check` job in the model CI.
maria: Action items: 1) anil add Grafana alert (ETA 1h). 2) kai extend router policy to disallow tokenizer-family-mismatch when `tool_call=true` for starter tier as a temporary rule (ETA end of day). 3) lee prototype rollout UI gate wireframe (ETA EOD). 4) sylvia add compat-check CI job and update matrix docs (ETA 2 days).
kai: For the router change, I'll add a soft-flag first: `router.fallback.strict_toolcall=true` in staging. We can run 24h and measure cost impact.
anil: Note: make sure we emit a telemetry tag on fallback event: `fallback_compat_reason=tokenizer_mismatch|context_trim|metadata_mismatch`. Tools currently only send `fallback_reason=variant_unavailable`.
sylvia: I'll update the events schema in the telemetry repo. Need to coordinate with analytics to map to billing dimensions.
maria: Also, for longer-term, we should enrich the compatibility matrix with the following columns: tokenizer_family, context_trim_behavior (left/right/truncate-kv), toolcall_protocol_version, kv_cache_format_version.
lee: And an automated cross-check job that runs weekly to detect drift across regions (some variants compiled with different tokenizer artifacts).
kai: Quick note: avoid adding too many hard rules for enterprise/dedicated customers — they expect pinned fallbacks. Introduce `fallback_policy_level` per tenant: `pin` (no substitution), `strict`, `economy`.
sylvia: Console default for new projects = `economy`, but onboarding flow should nudge teams to `strict` if they enable tool-calls.
maria: Can we capture this in a short blurb for product so they can update docs? I'll draft a 3-sentence note and post in #product.
lee: Testing pointer: include a tiny harness snippet in repo:
```
# parity test snippet
input = {"text": "call_tool:weather", "args": {"location": "SF"}}
for model in variants:
    tokens = model.tokenizer.encode(input)
    roundtrip = model.tokenizer.decode(tokens)
    assert roundtrip contains "call_tool"
```
kai: Nice. One more ops detail: when fallback occurs, preserve original request metadata in `original_request` field in the event log so we can reconstruct tool-call failures.
oncall-bot: New alert created: fallback_telemetry_inconsistency_euwest (linked to thread).
anil: I'll post a thin PR for the router flag in 30m. Kai will run it in staging.
maria: Thanks everyone — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review metrics post-staging run. If we see >0.5% increased cost for starter tier, rollback the flag. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Staging deploy scheduled: router-config-flag-2026-05-15T09:00Z
